rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed 3.75–4.00%, Dec hike ~75–82%; BoJ held 1.25% Oct 30 (8–1), Dec ~80%; ECB 2.50%, Dec hike >80%; RBA Nov 3 hike ~79–85%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%; BoC 2.50%, Dec ~45%; RBNZ 2.75%
rows.read: Most central banks still lean toward higher rates because of energy-driven inflation. The Bank of Japan held but said inflation has reached its goal, its clearest hint yet of a December hike. The Fed is still expected to hike in December, though falling US yields show markets testing that view.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US Q3 GDP 3.4% ann.; Japan Sep industrial output +2.2% m/m, retail sales +2.3% y/y (fc 3.3%); Nikkei −3%, Nasdaq 100 futures −1.4%; euro-area Q3 GDP 5:00 AM CT (fc 0.2% q/q)
rows.read: The US economy is still growing far faster than Europe's and Japan's. A slide in AI-linked shares is the new worry, because a lasting fall could hit spending and investment. Euro-area growth figures this morning show whether Europe is stalling.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Tokyo CPI 2.8% y/y (fc 2.7%), core 2.6%; BoJ FY2027 core forecast 2.6% (from 2.4%); Australia PPI +1.1% q/q (fc 1.0%), 3.6% y/y; euro-area flash CPI 5:00 AM CT (prior 3.8%); US ECI 7:30 AM CT (fc 0.8%)
rows.read: Energy keeps prices high nearly everywhere. Japan's central bank now says underlying inflation is at its goal, and Australian business prices are still climbing. Euro-area and US wage figures today show whether pressure is spreading beyond fuel.

rows.figure: US 10-year ~4.90%, 2-year ~4.57% (one-month lows); USD/JPY low ~157.12; USD/CHF ~0.8214; Nikkei −3%, KOSPI −5%
rows.read: Worries over AI spending sent shares sharply lower in Asia, and money ran to US Treasuries, the yen and the franc. The dollar did not gain, because falling US yields cut its rate edge. Talk of new US strikes on Iran adds a second source of nerves.

rows.figure: Brent ~$116.1 (+1%), WTI ~$103.3 (+1.3%); Brent ~+14% in October; OPEC+ meets Sunday
rows.read: Oil rose back near $116 on reports of new US military options against Iran, and is heading for a fourth monthly gain. That keeps helping exporters like Canada and Australia and costing importers like Japan and the euro area.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD and EUR (euro net short largest since March 2020), for GBP and AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold; next report Oct 30
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and the loonie's climb since Canada's rate hike puts those bets under pressure. Their bets against the euro are the largest in years, so good euro news could force them to buy it back. Fresh figures come Friday afternoon.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: French revenue vote Nov 3; S&P reviews France Nov 27; Lagarde: tools to counter disorderly bond moves; UK headroom £15bn
rows.read: France's budget fight is still unresolved and keeps a weight on the euro, with a vote on taxes due November 3. The European Central Bank says it has tools to calm disorderly bond selling. The UK Budget passed calmly, so British bonds and the pound took it in stride.
